stories_kpis.title: First Loss Prevention Colloquium Successfully Launched
stories_kpis.description: IVR organized its inaugural Loss Prevention Colloquium in Antwerp on November 4, 2024, attracting approximately 80 participants from Belgium, Netherlands, and Germany. This new recurring event complements the flagship annual congress and demonstrates IVR's expanding platform role in knowledge sharing and technical expertise dissemination across the inland waterway sector.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or digital transformation initiatives in the 2024 annual report. The organization focuses on traditional advocacy, regulatory participation, and knowledge exchange.
evidence: References to CESNI participation for standardization in technical areas and professional qualifications, but no AI or algorithmic systems mentioned.
Digitalization mentioned only in context of industry standards (CESNI work on digitalization in inland shipping), not organizational AI adoption.
Primary activities center on regulatory representation, loss prevention, and sectoral coordination through traditional committee and conference structures.

company_description: Carl Zeiss Meditec AG operates as a medical technology company in Germany, rest of Europe, North America, and Asia. It operates in two segments, Ophthalmology and Microsurgery. The Ophthalmology segment offers products and solutions for the diagnosis and treatment of chronic eye diseases, including slit lamps, refractometers, and tonometers; optical coherence tomography and fundus cameras for retina examination; functional glaucoma diagnostic devices (perimeters); surgical ophthalmology products comprising surgical microscopes, biometers, and phacoemulsification and vitrectomy equipment; intraocular lenses for cataract surgery; and systems and consumables for laser eye surgery that include the VISUMAX femtosecond laser, which enables minimally invasive correction of vision defects using lenticular extraction, as well as digital products for the storage, analysis, and sharing of clinical data.
